nodes.name: 03:40 daily (after 04)
nodes.notes: 03:40 — AFTER 04 has pulled contacts and written phones at 03:20. Identity resolution matches on the E.164 phone and nothing else, so running it first would resolve last night's phones against tonight's conversations and be a day behind forever.

parameters.query:
-- STEP 1 — resolve identity on phone (certain match).
--
-- THREE STATEMENTS, NOT ONE. This was a single statement with the customer
-- INSERT in a data-modifying CTE and the interaction UPDATE as the main query.
-- Postgres executes every sub-statement of a WITH against the SAME snapshot,
-- so the UPDATE could not see the customers the CTE had just inserted. The
-- observable result: the first run created 984 customers and linked 0
-- conversations, and the link only happened the NEXT night. Identity was
-- permanently one run behind, and on a fresh database it looked simply broken.
--
-- Separate statements get separate snapshots, so 1c sees 1a.

-- 1a · a customer for every phone we have never seen before.
INSERT INTO customers (primary_phone_e164, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT i.customer_phone_e164, min(i.started_at), max(i.started_at)
  FROM interactions i
 WHERE i.customer_id IS NULL
   AND i.customer_phone_e164 IS NOT NULL
   AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM customers c
                    WHERE c.primary_phone_e164 = i.customer_phone_e164)
 GROUP BY i.customer_phone_e164
ON CONFLICT (primary_phone_e164) DO NOTHING;

-- 1b · the audit trail: how this phone was matched, and how sure we are.
--
--      ONLY PHONES THIS PIPELINE ACTUALLY MATCHED. Driving this off the whole
--      `customers` table would stamp 'exact_phone, confidence 1.00' onto every
--      customer with a phone, including rows created by an import or by hand —
--      inventing a provenance record for a match that never happened. This
--      table IS the identity-resolution audit log (002); a fabricated row in
--      it makes a bad merge undiscoverable, which is the one job it has.
--
--      So: restricted to customers whose phone is carried by a conversation,
--      which is the only evidence this step ever has. Idempotent on
--      (kind, value), and separate from 1a for the snapshot reason above.
INSERT INTO customer_identities (customer_id, kind, value, method, confidence)
SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id, 'phone'::identity_kind, c.primary_phone_e164,
       'exact_phone'::match_method, 1.00
  FROM customers c
  JOIN interactions i ON i.customer_phone_e164 = c.primary_phone_e164
 WHERE c.primary_phone_e164 IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (kind, value) DO NOTHING;

-- 1c · attach every unlinked conversation carrying that phone.
UPDATE interactions i
   SET customer_id = c.customer_id, updated_at = now()
  FROM customers c
 WHERE i.customer_id IS NULL
   AND i.customer_phone_e164 = c.primary_phone_e164
RETURNING i.interaction_id, i.customer_id;

nodes.name: Resolve identity (phone)
nodes.notes: Phone match only — it is the one match that is certain. CRM-id and fuzzy-name matching are deliberately NOT automated: a wrong merge is expensive to undo and every match is written to customer_identities with its method and confidence.

parameters.query:
-- STEP 2 — turn agent promises extracted by pass 1 into follow_up rows,
-- then close any that a later interaction fulfilled.
INSERT INTO follow_ups (customer_id, agent_id, promised_in, promise_text, promised_at, due_at, channel)
SELECT i.customer_id, i.agent_id, i.interaction_id,
       p->>'promise',
       i.started_at,
       CASE WHEN p->>'due_hint' IS NOT NULL THEN i.started_at + interval '24 hours' END,
       i.channel
FROM interaction_analysis ia
JOIN interactions i ON i.interaction_id = ia.interaction_id
CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(
  coalesce(ia.raw_response->'promises_made_by_agent', '[]'::jsonb)) AS p
WHERE i.agent_id IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM follow_ups f
    WHERE f.promised_in = i.interaction_id AND f.promise_text = p->>'promise'
  )
-- RETURNING added (017). Without it a Postgres mutation hands n8n a single
-- {success:true} however many rows it touched, so the next node cannot tell
-- 'wrote 40 promises' from 'wrote none' -- and check_workflow_json rejects
-- the shape outright. Nothing downstream reads these rows; they exist so a
-- run leaves a countable trace.
RETURNING follow_up_id, promised_in, promise_text, due_at;

-- STEP 3 — close promises that a later outbound contact fulfilled.
UPDATE follow_ups f
SET fulfilled_in = nxt.interaction_id,
    fulfilled_at = nxt.started_at,
    hours_to_fulfil = round(extract(epoch from (nxt.started_at - f.promised_at))/3600.0, 2),
    status = CASE
      WHEN nxt.started_at <= coalesce(f.due_at, f.promised_at + interval '24 hours')
        THEN 'fulfilled' ELSE 'late' END,
    updated_at = now()
FROM LATERAL (
  SELECT i.interaction_id, i.started_at
  FROM interactions i
  WHERE i.customer_id = f.customer_id
    AND i.started_at > f.promised_at
    AND i.agent_id = f.agent_id
  ORDER BY i.started_at
  LIMIT 1
) nxt
WHERE f.status = 'open';

-- Anything still open past its deadline is a missed promise, not a pending one.
UPDATE follow_ups
SET status = 'missed', updated_at = now()
WHERE status = 'open'
  AND coalesce(due_at, promised_at + interval '48 hours') < now()
-- RETURNING added (017). Without it a Postgres mutation hands n8n a single
-- {success:true} however many rows it touched, so the next node cannot tell
-- 'wrote 40 promises' from 'wrote none' -- and check_workflow_json rejects
-- the shape outright. Nothing downstream reads these rows; they exist so a
-- run leaves a countable trace.
RETURNING follow_up_id, status, fulfilled_at;

nodes.name: Rebuild customer_metrics
nodes.notes: Truncate and rebuild. customer_metrics is fully derived, so it can always be dropped and recomputed — which is what stops a wrong dashboard number from becoming permanent.

parameters.query:
-- STEP 2 — who handled each conversation (migration 018).
--
-- Runs BEFORE promises are materialised because "Materialise promises" filters
-- on `i.agent_id IS NOT NULL`. While agent_id was NULL everywhere that filter
-- matched zero rows on every run, which is the entire reason `follow_ups` sat
-- at 0 while pass 1 had been extracting promises the whole time.
--
-- Idempotent and cheap: every UPDATE inside is guarded by IS DISTINCT FROM, so
-- a night that changes nothing writes nothing.
SELECT link_agent_attribution() AS attribution;
